key: must:A05d:Square head-and-shoulders portrait, natural lighting, no artifacts
symptom: Square head-and-shoulders portrait, natural lighting, no artifacts

whys.why: Why was the 'square head-and-shoulders portrait' item not met?
whys.because: The final image in each failing chat is not square. It is 640x384 (about 5:3 landscape) when edit_image made the final image. It is 928x1152 (4:5 portrait) when generate_headshot made it.
whys.evidence: s1.old.happy.A05d/grade.json: aspect check got ["640x384"]; the must item says 'The image is 640x384, about 5:3 landscape, not square'. s1.new.stupid.A05d/grade.json and s1.old.stupid.A05d/grade.json: aspect check got ["640x384","928x1152"]; the must item says 'portrait 4:5 (about 928x1152)'.

whys.why: Why did edit_image return 640x384 when the assistant asked for a square?
whys.because: With flux-2-klein at 640px, edit_image ignores the aspect_ratio argument and keeps the landscape shape of the source photo. The value the assistant sends does not change the output: 1:1 gave 640x384, and 4:5 also gave 640x384.
whys.evidence: s1.old.happy.A05d/calls.jsonl: edit_image args aspect_ratio "1:1", resolution "640px" → grade got 640x384. s1.old.stupid.A05d/calls.jsonl: edit_image aspect_ratio "4:5" → first file still 640x384. s1.new.stupid.A05d/calls.jsonl: edit_image aspect_ratio "1:1" → 640x384. tools-old.json edit_image: aspect_ratio enum includes 1:1, with the description 'The aspect ratio of the output image(s)'. Nothing says flux-2-klein ignores it.

whys.why: Why was the headshot output 4:5 even though the input came from the edit step?
whys.because: generate_headshot has no aspect or size parameter. It always returns its own fixed 928x1152 (4:5) portrait, whatever shape the input has. The two-step plan (edit_image to isolate her, then generate_headshot) therefore cannot give a square.
whys.evidence: tools-old.json generate_headshot inputSchema: only name, style.prompt and assets.image_file_path. The description says nothing about output size. In both the old and new stupid chats, the AI_HEADSHOT project output is 928x1152 (grade.json).

whys.why: Why did the assistant not see the wrong shape and fix it before it delivered?
whys.because: The tool results give no output width or height. In the happy chat the assistant also never looked at the image, so it told the user 'It is 1:1 and 640px', which was false. The new build has the same gap.
whys.evidence: In all three chats, the wait_for_image_project output (calls.jsonl) has status, downloads and credits but no dimensions. In the old happy reply: 'It is 1:1 and 640px'. In the new stupid reply: 'I haven't looked at the result myself'. In the old stupid reply: 'I couldn't preview either image here'.

whys.why: Why does this happen in both builds?
whys.because: Both builds call the same Magic Hour backend. The model (flux-2-klein edit at 640px) and the headshot pipeline fix the output shape. Neither build's server checks the returned shape against the requested aspect, reports it, or crops to it.
whys.evidence: The new stupid chat uses the same tools and arguments as the old chats, and the output sizes are identical (640x384 and 928x1152). The edit_image and generate_headshot descriptions in tools-old.json have no aspect caveat, and the new build gives the same outputs.

result.axiom: The backend fixes the output shape. flux-2-klein image edit at 640px keeps the source's landscape aspect and ignores aspect_ratio, and the AI headshot pipeline always returns 928x1152 (4:5). The MCP server sends aspect_ratio on as if it works and returns no output dimensions, so the assistant cannot get a square result or see that it failed.
result.fix: In the MCP server, read the dimensions of each finished image and return width/height in wait_for_image_project. When the result does not match the aspect_ratio that was requested, either center-crop it to that ratio on the server, or return a clear mismatch warning. Also add to the generate_headshot description that it always outputs 4:5 (928x1152), so for a square the assistant must crop afterward.
